title: Mobile Money in Tanzania
eligible_reason: Structural demand model (simulated GMM probit for transfer and transportation-storage needs) identified from a single, unanticipated, network-wide transaction-fee increase; no unit-by-time panel regression with a binary staggered treatment. The shipped transaction data are synthetic.
design_notes: Package is MATLAB/C code for GMM estimation (estimate.m, estimate_cashout.m, probit.c, moments.c) plus WTP and pricing counterfactuals. The fee increase occurs at one common date for all users, so there is no adoption-date variation. The regression inventory is empty (no OLS/FE regressions in the code).
data_files_note: readme.txt lists dataTran.mat and data_cashout.mat (42 x 100,000 transfers per individual) as 'Synthetic data'; 'Real data' are only the transfer-amount grid, estimated extra cash-out fees and the final parameter vectors.
data_provenance_note: Individual transaction data replaced by simulated draws; real data are proprietary telecom records.
software_notes: MATLAB with C mex moment functions.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally; abstract (data/frame/mksc.jsonl) and package readme read. The full-text 'difference in difference' flag likely refers to a descriptive before/after comparison around the fee change; with one common date it cannot be staggered.
